verses.text: Now it came to pass in the days when the judges ruled. There was a famine (no food) in the land. And a certain man of Bethlehemjudah went to sojourn (live for a while) in Moab. He went with his wife, and his 2 sons.

And the name of the man was Elimelech. The name of his wife was Naomi. The names of his 2 sons were Mahlon and Chilion. They were Ephrathites of Bethlehemjudah. And they came into the country of Moab, and continued there.
And Elimelech, Naomi's husband, died. And Naomi was left, and her 2 sons.
And they took them wives of the women of Moab. The name of the one was Orpah, and the name of the other Ruth. And they dwelt (lived) there about 10 years.
And Mahlon and Chilion died also both of them. And the woman was left of her 2 sons and her husband.

Then Naomi arose (got up) with her daughters in law, to return from Moab. For she had heard in the country of Moab some news. She heard how the LORD had visited (cared for) His people in giving them bread.
So Naomi went forth (out) out of the place where she was. Her 2 daughters in law went with her. And they went on the way to return to the land of Judah.
And Naomi said to her 2 daughters in law: Go, return each to her mother's house. The LORD deal kindly with you. You have dealt kindly with the dead, and with me.
The LORD grant you that you may find rest. May each of you find rest in the house of her husband. Then Naomi kissed them. And they lifted up their voice, and wept.
And they said to Naomi: Surely we will return with you to your people.
And Naomi said: Turn again, my daughters. Why will you go with me? Are there yet any more sons in my womb? Could they be your husbands?
Turn again, my daughters, go your way. For I am too old to have a husband. I might say: I have hope. I might have a husband also to night. I might also bear (give birth to) sons.

Would you tarry (wait) for them till they were grown? Would you stay for them from having husbands? No, my daughters. For it grieves me much for your sakes. The hand of the LORD is gone out against me.
And they lifted up their voice, and wept again. And Orpah kissed her mother in law. But Ruth clave (held tight) to her.
And Naomi said: Look, your sister in law is gone back to her people. She has gone back to her gods. Return after your sister in law.

And Ruth said: Intreat (beg) me not to leave you, or to return from following after you. For whither (where) you go, I will go. And where you lodge (stay), I will lodge (stay). Your people shall be my people, and your God my God.
Where you die, will I die, and there will I be buried. Only death will part you and me. If anything else does, the LORD do so to me, and more also.
Naomi saw that Ruth was stedfastly minded (firmly decided) to go with her. Then Naomi left speaking to her.
So the 2 of them went until they came to Bethlehem. And it came to pass, when they were come to Bethlehem. All the city was moved about them, and they said: Is this Naomi?
And Naomi said to them: Call me not Naomi (pleasant). Call me Mara (bitter). For the Almighty has dealt very bitterly with me.
I went out full, and the LORD has brought me home again empty. Why then call me Naomi (pleasant)? The LORD has testified against me. And the Almighty has afflicted (hurt) me.
So Naomi returned, and Ruth the Moabitess, her daughter in law, with her. They returned out of the country of Moab. And they came to Bethlehem in the beginning of barley harvest.

verses.text: And Naomi had a kinsman (relative) of her husband's, a mighty man of wealth. He was of the family of Elimelech. And his name was Boaz.

And Ruth the Moabitess said to Naomi: Let me now go to the field. Let me glean (pick up the leftover) ears of corn (grain). I will glean after him in whose sight I shall find grace (kindness). And Naomi said to her: Go, my daughter.

And Ruth went, and came, and gleaned (picked up leftover grain) in the field after the reapers (harvest workers). And her hap (chance) was to light on (come to) a part of the field of Boaz. Boaz was of the kindred (family) of Elimelech.
And look, Boaz came from Bethlehem, and said to the reapers (harvest workers): The LORD be with you. And they answered him: The LORD bless you.
Then Boaz said to his servant that was set over the reapers (harvest workers): Whose damsel (young woman) is this?
And the servant that was set over the reapers (harvest workers) answered and said: It is the Moabitish damsel (young woman from Moab). She came back with Naomi out of the country of Moab.

And she said: I pray you (please), let me glean (pick up leftover grain) and gather. Let me gather after the reapers among the sheaves (bundles). So she came, and has continued even from the morning until now. She only tarried (rested) a little in the house.
Then Boaz said to Ruth: Hear, my daughter. Do not go to glean (pick up leftover grain) in another field. Neither go from here. But abide (stay) here fast (close) by my maidens (young women workers).

Let your eyes be on the field that they reap (harvest). Go after them. Have I not charged (told) the young men that they shall not touch you? And when you are thirsty, go to the vessels (jars). Drink of that which the young men have drawn.

Then Ruth fell on her face, and bowed herself to the ground. She said to Boaz: Why have I found grace (kindness) in your eyes? Why should you take knowledge of (notice) me? For I am a stranger (foreigner).

And Boaz answered and said to her: It has fully been showed me all that you have done. You did it for your mother in law since the death of your husband. You have left your father and your mother. You left the land of your nativity (birth). You are come to a people which you knew not before.
The LORD recompense (reward) your work. A full reward be given you of the LORD God of Israel. You are come to trust under His wings.

Then Ruth said: Let me find favour in your sight, my lord. For you have comforted me, and you have spoken friendly to your handmaid (servant). Yet I am not like one of your handmaidens (women servants).

And Boaz said to her: At mealtime come here, and eat of the bread. Dip your morsel (piece of bread) in the vinegar (sour wine). And she sat beside the reapers (harvest workers). And Boaz reached her parched corn (roasted grain). And she did eat, and was sufficed (full), and left some.
And Ruth was risen up to glean (pick up leftover grain). Then Boaz commanded his young men, saying: Let her glean even among the sheaves (bundles). And reproach her not (do not shame her).
And let fall also some of the handfuls of purpose for her. Leave them, so that she may glean (pick) them. And rebuke her not (do not scold her).
So Ruth gleaned (picked up leftover grain) in the field until evening. She beat out that she had gleaned (picked up). And it was about an ephah (about 5 gallons) of barley.

And Ruth took it up, and went into the city. And her mother in law saw what she had gleaned (picked up). And Ruth brought forth (out) what she had reserved (saved). She gave it to Naomi after she was sufficed (full).

And her mother in law said to her: Where have you gleaned (picked up grain) to day (today)? And where did you work? Blessed be he that did take knowledge of (notice) you. And Ruth showed her mother in law with whom she had worked. She said: The man's name with whom I worked to day (today) is Boaz.

And Naomi said to her daughter in law: Blessed be he of the LORD. The LORD has not left off His kindness to the living and the dead. And Naomi said to her: The man is near of kin (closely related) to us. He is one of our next kinsmen (closest relatives).
And Ruth the Moabitess said: He said to me also: You shall keep fast (close) by my young men. Stay until they have ended all my harvest.
And Naomi said to Ruth her daughter in law: It is good, my daughter. Go out with his maidens (young women workers). Then they will not meet you in any other field.

So Ruth kept fast (close) by the maidens (young women workers) of Boaz to glean (pick up leftover grain). She gleaned to the end of barley harvest and of wheat harvest. And she dwelt (lived) with her mother in law.

verses.text: Then Naomi her mother in law said to Ruth: My daughter, shall I not seek (look for) rest for you? Then it may be well with you.

And now is not Boaz of our kindred (family)? You were with his maidens (young women workers). Look, he winnows (separates the grain from the chaff) barley to night. He winnows it in the threshingfloor (place where grain is beaten out).

Wash yourself therefore, and anoint (put perfumed oil on) yourself. Put your raiment (clothing) upon you, and go down to the floor (threshing floor). But do not make yourself known to the man. Wait until he has done eating and drinking.
And it shall be, when he lies down, you shall mark (notice) the place. And you shall go in, and uncover his feet, and lay down. And he will tell you what you shall do.
And Ruth said to her: All that you say to me I will do.
And Ruth went down to the floor (threshing floor). She did according to all that her mother in law bade (told) her.
And Boaz had eaten and drunk, and his heart was merry (happy). He went to lie down at the end of the heap of corn (grain). And Ruth came softly (quietly), and uncovered his feet, and laid her down.
And it came to pass at midnight. The man was afraid, and turned himself. And look, a woman lay at his feet.

And Boaz said: Who are you? And she answered: I am Ruth your handmaid (servant). Spread therefore your skirt (the edge of your cloak) over your handmaid (servant). For you are a near kinsman (close relative).
And Boaz said: Blessed be you of the LORD, my daughter. For you have showed more kindness in the latter end than at the beginning. For you followed not young men, whether poor or rich.
And now, my daughter, fear not. I will do to you all that you require (ask). For all the city of my people does know this: you are a virtuous (good and honorable) woman.
And now it is true that I am your near kinsman (close relative). However, there is a kinsman (relative) nearer than I.

Tarry (stay) this night, and it shall be in the morning. He may perform to you the part of a kinsman (relative). If so, well, let him do the kinsman's part. But he may not do the part of a kinsman to you. Then I will do the part of a kinsman, as the LORD lives. Lie down until the morning.
And Ruth lay at his feet until the morning. And she rose up before one could know another. And Boaz said: Let it not be known that a woman came into the floor (threshing floor).
Also Boaz said: Bring the vail (shawl) that you have upon you, and hold it. And when she held it, he measured 6 measures of barley. He laid it on her. And she went into the city.
And Ruth came to her mother in law. Naomi said: Who are you, my daughter? And Ruth told her all that the man had done to her.
And Ruth said: These 6 measures of barley he gave me. For he said to me: Go not empty to your mother in law.
Then Naomi said: Sit still, my daughter, until you know how the matter will fall (turn out). For the man will not be in rest. He will finish the thing this day.

verses.text: Then Boaz went up to the gate, and sat him down there. And look, the kinsman (relative) came by. Boaz had spoken of him. Boaz said to him: Ho, such a one (friend)! Turn aside, sit down here. And he turned aside, and sat down.
And Boaz took 10 men of the elders of the city, and said: Sit down here. And they sat down.
And Boaz said to the kinsman (relative): Naomi is come again out of the country of Moab. She sells a parcel (piece) of land, which was our brother Elimelech's.

And I thought to advertise (tell) you. I say: Buy it before the inhabitants (people living here), and before the elders of my people. If you will redeem (buy back) it, redeem it. But you may not redeem it. Then tell me, so that I may know. For there is none to redeem it beside you, and I am after you. And he said: I will redeem (buy back) it.

Then Boaz said: You will buy the field of the hand of Naomi. On that day you must buy it also of Ruth the Moabitess. She is the wife of the dead. You must raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance (property).
And the kinsman (relative) said: I cannot redeem (buy back) it for myself. Lest (or else) I mar (ruin) my own inheritance (property). You redeem my right to yourself, for I cannot redeem it.

Now this was the manner (custom) in former time in Israel. It was the custom for redeeming (buying back) and for changing, to confirm all things. A man plucked off his shoe, and gave it to his neighbour. And this was a testimony (proof) in Israel.
Therefore the kinsman (relative) said to Boaz: Buy it for yourself. So he drew off his shoe.
And Boaz said to the elders, and to all the people: You are witnesses this day. I have bought all that was Elimelech's, of the hand of Naomi. I have bought all that was Chilion's and Mahlon's.

Moreover (also) I have purchased Ruth the Moabitess to be my wife. She was the wife of Mahlon. I will raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance (property). Then the dead man's name will not be cut off from his brethren (brothers). It will not be cut off from the gate of his place. You are witnesses this day.

And all the people that were in the gate, and the elders, said: We are witnesses. A woman is come into your house. The LORD make her like Rachel and like Leah. Those two did build the house of Israel. And do worthily in Ephratah, and be famous in Bethlehem.

And let your house be like the house of Pharez. Tamar bare (gave birth to) Pharez to Judah. Let your house come from the seed (children) the LORD shall give you. He will give them by this young woman.
So Boaz took Ruth, and she was his wife. And when he went in to her, the LORD gave her conception (made her pregnant). And she bare (gave birth to) a son.
And the women said to Naomi: Blessed be the LORD. He has not left you this day without a kinsman (redeemer). May his name be famous in Israel.

And he shall be to you a restorer of your life. He shall be a nourisher (one who cares for you) of your old age. For your daughter in law, which loves you, has born him. She is better to you than 7 sons.
And Naomi took the child, and laid it in her bosom (lap). And she became nurse (caretaker) to it.
And the women her neighbours gave it a name, saying: There is a son born to Naomi. And they called his name Obed. He is the father of Jesse, the father of David.
Now these are the generations (family line) of Pharez: Pharez begat (became the father of) Hezron,
And Hezron begat (became the father of) Ram, and Ram begat (became the father of) Amminadab,
And Amminadab begat (became the father of) Nahshon, and Nahshon begat (became the father of) Salmon,
And Salmon begat (became the father of) Boaz, and Boaz begat (became the father of) Obed,
And Obed begat (became the father of) Jesse, and Jesse begat (became the father of) David.
